html:
Amanullah Khan was emir and then king of Afghanistan from 1919 to 1929, who won full independence for the country and tried to modernise it at speed. He was born in 1892 near Kabul.

He led the Third Anglo-Afghan War in his first year on the throne. He then gave Afghanistan its first constitution in 1923, opened schools for girls, and with his wife Queen Soraya appeared unveiled in public. After a grand tour of Europe in 1927 and 1928, he ordered Western dress in Kabul and limits on the clergy.

Religious leaders and tribes rose against him, and in January 1929 he abdicated and fled. He died in exile in Zurich in 1960. His reforms were a model for later rulers such as Zahir Shah, whose 1964 constitution took up some of them, and his story is often cited as a warning about change imposed from the top, as in the Saur Revolution.
